source.title: Weak-to-Strong On-Policy Distillation
source.authors: Fangxu Yu; Zinan Lin; Xiao-Dong Liu; Wei-Jia Xu; Michael Xu; Tianyi Zhou; Jianfeng Gao

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests weak-to-strong improvement with a different method: the strong student is trained by on-policy distillation from a proxy teacher made from weak-model logit contrasts, rather than by ordinary fine-tuning on weak labels.
record.gate_note: The paper reports benchmark outcomes for W2S-OPD, direct OPD and reference models, plus an out-of-domain evaluation and an amplification-coefficient sweep. The paper does not calculate PGR. Token-distribution and reasoning-episode analyses describe the contrast signals but are not separate outcomes on the claim's benchmark-performance measures.
record.test_reason: An 8B student is trained only on signals from smaller 4B/0.6B models, and its accuracy is compared with the weak sources, the student base and direct OPD. This tests V1/V2/V3 by a different method (logit-contrast on-policy distillation, not fine-tuning on weak labels). There is no strong ceiling, so PGR cannot be computed.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude W2S-OPD beats direct OPD and lifts the student above the weak domain teacher. But that holds on math only; on code it narrows the gap without passing the teacher. They also say it improves the student when all sources are weaker, and preserves or enhances out-of-domain ability.
record.recipe_differences: Uses on-policy token-distribution distillation with reverse KL toward a proxy teacher synthesized from positive-minus-negative model logits and anchored to the strong student's base model. It is not ordinary fine-tuning on labels generated by a weak supervisor.
record.method_sensitivity: Amplification coefficient α: small values inject little signal; larger values improve results up to a point, after which performance declines on most benchmarks. Contrast-pair choice and task also change the measured outcome.

fits_no_version.finding: The top-1% highest-Δ tokens concentrate on different Schoenfeld episodes: Plan/Monitor for the post-RL and hint contrasts, Analyze/Implement for the scale contrast (Table 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different weak-model contrast pairs transfer different reasoning-episode signals to the strong student.

record.problems: The study uses Qwen3 models and reports no uncertainty estimates. It does not calculate PGR or test the original weak-label fine-tuning recipe, so its results are evidence for a related weak-to-strong method rather than a direct replication of the stated measure.

untested.parts: PGR (no strong-ceiling 8B model trained on ground truth or RL). Not tested with the original fine-tune-on-weak-labels recipe beyond SFT/OPD baselines.
Auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling and loss variants are not tested. No uncertainty or repeated seeds.
Only the Qwen3 family and an 8B student. Student size is not varied. No chess or reward modelling. Only two negative-model sizes.
Entirely untested. The OOD evaluation reports no PGR. There is no analysis of exploitation or of error similarity.
No theory on when a student must beat its supervisor; Appendix B only reinterprets the objective.

missing.what: SFT and direct-OPD results vs the 4B-RL teacher: math 45.7/46.5 (single), 46.8/46.5 (multi) vs 48.8; code 59.7/58.7 and 60.4/59.5 vs 61.5. This is the naive weak-supervisor baseline for V1.
W2S-OPD vs student base in the pre/post-RL setting (math 17.0→51.8, code 57.6→60.9)
Per-step training curves: W2S-OPD above OPD throughout training

record.verdict_notes: The 'weak' supervisor in the pre/post-RL setting is smaller but far task-stronger than the 8B base (48.8 vs 17.0 math), unlike the original setup. The proxy teacher also embeds the student's own base logits. Treat the evidence as a related weak-to-strong method, not a PGR replication. The reader's V4 'challenges' label is removed: the OOD rows carry no PGR. Single run, no error bars. Preprint.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the original recipe of fine-tuning on labels produced by a weaker model or report PGR. Tests performance relative to weak reference models using logit-contrast on-policy distillation.
Tests the proxy-teacher/logit-contrast method against direct OPD and varies its amplification coefficient; does not separately test auxiliary confidence loss or other named loss variants.
Tests Qwen3 0.6B, 4B and 8B settings across math and code benchmarks and analyzes contrast-token patterns. Does not test multiple model families or chess/reward modelling.

Evaluates generalization to two out-of-domain benchmarks. Does not test whether students exploit what supervisors cannot check, whether gains shrink when weak and strong models err alike, or report PGR under shift.
No theoretical conditions under which a student must beat its supervisor are tested.
No vision or other non-language modality is tested.

relation.reason: The study compares trained students with weak sources, student initialization, SFT and direct OPD, and varies tasks, contrast pairs and amplification.

tranche.reason: Logit-contrast on-policy distillation tests improvement from weaker supervision with a different method and accuracy measure; it does not reproduce the original weak-label fine-tuning and PGR setup.

source_check.notes: No strong ceiling, PGR or empirical uncertainty is reported; evidence uses accuracy comparisons. Hint contrasts additionally require reference-solution information, and Table 3's 4B math average is 14.9 despite Figure 1 displaying 15.4.

statements.correction: Table 2: code teacher=61.5; student base=57.6; strong ceiling=not reported; PGR=not reported.
statements.problem: The teacher exceeds the student base, but that alone does not make PGR undefined: its denominator uses the strong ceiling, which this study does not report.

statements.correction: Table 2, single teacher: HumanEval+=83.1→84.8; MBPP+=71.2→72.4; code average=58.7→60.9; all positive gains over OPD; label=limits_scope.
statements.problem: The smaller code gains are accurate, but they do not establish absent or reversed method gains for this study; its contribution warrants limits_scope rather than challenges.
